forced_preflight_collision.method: A fixture-only PATH wrapper waits at the real mv/git-mv call until all four workers have completed preflight, collision checks, digest and mtime pinning. It then execs /usr/bin/mv or /usr/bin/git unchanged. No receipt engine substitution, target modification, test hook, or tool-source modification is used. All workers also request an unreceipted fresh-note.txt sentinel.

log_audit.exit_codes: All 72 invocations returned 3: overlapping requests encounter refusals/staging failures, or the deliberately unreceipted sentinel is refused. This is expected fail-closed behavior, not a defect.

observations_not_counted_as_defects.observation: Parent/child overlap can create an extra nested directory in quarantine when the child creates the parent's destination between collision check and mv. The parent digest/mtime checks abort; remaining payloads stay recoverable, and independently deleted children had their own successful receipt checks.
observations_not_counted_as_defects.classification: Fail-closed refusal; no unsafe deletion, so not a defect under the round rules.

observations_not_counted_as_defects.observation: Two of three natural tracked-file trials emitted index-cleanup-skipped and retained one nonexistent quarantine path in the Git index. The actual payload deletion was authorized. The implementation explicitly documents index cleanup as best-effort and emits a warning; it does not silently claim cleanup succeeded.
observations_not_counted_as_defects.classification: Documented best-effort operational caveat; not a false SAFE/DELETE finding. A per-repository lock or retry could improve index tidiness if desired.
